#Categorical Var. Fun Stats
category_summary <- function(df, var) {
  tab <- table(df[[var]])
  data.frame(
    Variable      = var,
    N_Categories  = length(tab),
    Most_Common   = names(tab)[which.max(tab)],
    N_Most_Common = max(tab),
    Least_Common  = names(tab)[which.min(tab)],
    N_Least_Common = min(tab),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}
cat_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cat_cols, function(x) category_summary(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers, x)))

print(cat_summary)

#Removing MPG_bin for modeling purposes
auto_omit <- dplyr::select(auto_omit, -MPG_bin)
auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers <- dplyr::select(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers, -MPG_bin)

#Feature Selection and Ojective 1 Model ##Using Domain Knowledge to remove Attributes - City and Highway MPG have high correlation and measure very similar things - Engine HP and Cylinder are closely related - Vehicle Style and Size are also - No. of Doors could also be connected to Style - Market Category and Make tend to be closely related as well.

Removing Highway.MPG, Engine.Cylinder, Vehicle.Size, No. of Doors, Make (The new DF will be created up above)

# Full Model (all predictors) 
full.model <- lm(MSRP ~ ., data = auto_omit_reduced)
full.model_noout <- lm(MSRP ~ ., data = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)

# Null Model (only intercept)
null.model <- lm(MSRP ~ 1, data = auto_omit_reduced)
null.model_noout <- lm(MSRP ~ 1, data = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)

# Forward Selection 
#MSRP ~ Market.Category + Engine.HP + Driven_Wheels + Transmission.Type + Vehicle.Style + city.mpg + Engine.Fuel.Type + Year #AIC 247273.4 (Noout)
forward <- step(null.model, scope = formula(full.model), direction = "forward")

  labs(title="Residuals vs Fitted | glmnet")

  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  labs(title="QQ Plot of Residuals")

##Log Transforming MSRP We will transform the MSRP to resolve some assumption violations. The outliers are so strong that, we’ve decided to see what it looks like when you transfrom the log transform the msrp

# Full Model (all predictors) -- LOG TRANSFORMATION
full.model_log <- lm(log(MSRP) ~ ., data = auto_omit_reduced)
full.model_noout_log <- lm(log(MSRP) ~ ., data = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)

# Null Model (only intercept) -- LOG TRANSFORMATION
null.model_log <- lm(log(MSRP) ~ 1, data = auto_omit_reduced)
null.model_noout_log <- lm(log(MSRP) ~ 1, data = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)

forward_log <- step(null.model_log, scope = formula(full.model_log), direction = "forward")

# Predict and get residuals for log(MSRP)
preds_noout_log <- predict(glmnet_noout_log.fit, newdata = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)
residuals_noout_log <- log(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers$MSRP) - preds_noout_log
df_resid_noout_log <- data.frame(Fitted = as.numeric(preds_noout_log), Residuals = as.numeric(residuals_noout_log))

# Residuals vs Fitted for log model
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(df_resid_noout_log, aes(x=Fitted, y=Residuals)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept=0, linetype="dashed", color="red") +
  labs(title = "Residuals vs Fitted | glmnet log(MSRP)")

# QQ Plot for log residuals
ggplot(data.frame(resid = residuals_noout_log), aes(sample = resid)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  labs(title = "QQ Plot of Residuals (log MSRP)")

#Objective 2 Complex MLR and Non-Parametric ##EDA for Non-Parametric model #Adding interactions Engine.hpVehicle.Style, Engine.HPTransmission.Type, city.mpg*Engine.Fuel.Type, Engine.hp^2, and city.mpg^2

ggplot(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers, aes(x=Engine.HP, y=log(MSRP))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method='lm')
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

#Evidence of Interaction HP and Vehicle Style
ggplot(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers, aes(x = Engine.HP, y = MSRP, color = Vehicle.Style)) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(title = "HP vs MSRP by Vehicle Style")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

m1 <- lm(MSRP ~ Engine.HP + Vehicle.Style, data = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)
m2 <- lm(MSRP ~ Engine.HP * Vehicle.Style, data = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)  # add interaction
anova(m1, m2) #Evidence that the interaction is significant
## Analysis of Variance Table
## 
## Model 1: MSRP ~ Engine.HP + Vehicle.Style
## Model 2: MSRP ~ Engine.HP * Vehicle.Style
##   Res.Df        RSS Df Sum of Sq      F    Pr(>F)    
## 1  11679 5.2915e+12                                  
## 2  11664 4.6555e+12 15  6.36e+11 106.23 < 2.2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#Evidence of Interaction HP and Transmission Type
ggplot(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers, aes(x = Engine.HP, y = MSRP, color = Transmission.Type)) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(title = "HP vs MSRP by Transmission")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

m1 <- lm(MSRP ~ Engine.HP + Transmission.Type, data = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)
m2 <- lm(MSRP ~ Engine.HP * Transmission.Type, data = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)  # add interaction
anova(m1, m2) #Evidence that the interaction is significant
## Analysis of Variance Table
## 
## Model 1: MSRP ~ Engine.HP + Transmission.Type
## Model 2: MSRP ~ Engine.HP * Transmission.Type
##   Res.Df        RSS Df  Sum of Sq      F    Pr(>F)    
## 1  11690 5.5939e+12                                   
## 2  11686 5.2802e+12  4 3.1371e+11 173.57 < 2.2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#Fuel Type defnitely has an effect
ggplot(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers, aes(x = city.mpg, y = MSRP, color = Engine.Fuel.Type)) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(title = "HP vs MSRP by Vehicle Style")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

data_no_electric <- filter(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers, Engine.Fuel.Type != "electric")

ggplot(data_no_electric, aes(x = city.mpg, y = MSRP, color = Engine.Fuel.Type)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(title = "City MPG vs MSRP by Fuel Type")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

#Polynomial for HP?
ggplot(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers, aes(x=Engine.HP, y=log(MSRP))) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method='loess')
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

mod_linear <- lm(log(MSRP) ~ Engine.HP, data = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)
mod_quad   <- lm(log(MSRP) ~ Engine.HP + I(Engine.HP^2), data = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)

# Comparing models AIC is lower for quad, showing that its
AIC(mod_linear, mod_quad)
##            df      AIC
## mod_linear  3 28362.31
## mod_quad    4 27925.25
#PolyNomial for mpg?
ggplot(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers, aes(x=city.mpg, y=log(MSRP))) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method='loess')
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

##Checkwithout electric
ggplot(data_no_electric, aes(x=Engine.HP, y=log(MSRP))) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method='loess')
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

mod_linear <- lm(log(MSRP) ~ city.mpg, data = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)
mod_quad   <- lm(log(MSRP) ~ city.mpg + I(city.mpg^2), data = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)

# Comparing models AIC is lower for quad, showing that its significant to keep it in the model
AIC(mod_linear, mod_quad)
##            df      AIC
## mod_linear  3 34910.15
## mod_quad    4 34875.85

#Complex Model

# Full model with main effects, polynomial, and interactions
complex_model <- lm(
  log(MSRP) ~ 
    Year +
    Market.Category +
    Engine.Fuel.Type +
    Vehicle.Style +
    Transmission.Type +
    Driven_Wheels +
    city.mpg +
    Engine.HP +
    I(Engine.HP^2) +  # Quadratic (polynomial)
    Engine.HP:Vehicle.Style +
    Engine.HP:Transmission.Type +
    city.mpg:Engine.Fuel.Type,
  data = auto_omit_reduced
)

complex_model_noout <- lm(
  log(MSRP) ~ 
    Year +
    Market.Category +
    Engine.Fuel.Type +
    Vehicle.Style +
    Transmission.Type +
    Driven_Wheels +
    city.mpg +
    Engine.HP +
    I(Engine.HP^2) +  # Quadratic (polynomial)
    Engine.HP:Vehicle.Style +
    Engine.HP:Transmission.Type +
    city.mpg:Engine.Fuel.Type,
  data = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers
)

AIC(complex_model)
## [1] 12831.53
AIC(complex_model_noout)
## [1] 12522.69
summary(complex_model_noout)

#KNN_Full
# 1. Select features
features <- c("Year", "Market.Category", "Engine.HP", "Engine.Fuel.Type", 
              "city.mpg", "Vehicle.Style", "Transmission.Type", "Driven_Wheels")
knn_data <- auto_omit_reduced %>% select(MSRP, all_of(features))

# 2. Train/test split
set.seed(123)
idx <- createDataPartition(knn_data$MSRP, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_set <- knn_data[idx, ]
test_set  <- knn_data[-idx, ]

# 3. Create dummy variables (one-hot encoding for categorical predictors)
dummies   <- dummyVars(MSRP ~ ., data = train_set)
train_enc <- predict(dummies, newdata = train_set)
test_enc  <- predict(dummies, newdata = test_set)
train_enc <- data.frame(MSRP = train_set$MSRP, train_enc)
test_enc  <- data.frame(MSRP = test_set$MSRP, test_enc)

# 4. Center/scale all numeric variables
preproc     <- preProcess(train_enc, method = c("center", "scale"))
## Warning in preProcess.default(train_enc, method = c("center", "scale")): These
## variables have zero variances:
## Market.Category.Crossover.Exotic.Luxury.Performance,
## Market.Category.Performance.Hybrid
train_prep  <- predict(preproc, newdata = train_enc)
test_prep   <- predict(preproc, newdata = test_enc)

# 5. Fit KNN on processed data
set.seed(123)
knn_fit <- train(
  MSRP ~ .,
  data = train_prep,
  method = "knn",
  tuneLength = 10,
  trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5)
)
print(knn_fit)
## k-Nearest Neighbors 
## 
## 9454 samples
##  109 predictor
## 
## No pre-processing
## Resampling: Cross-Validated (5 fold) 
## Summary of sample sizes: 7564, 7562, 7564, 7564, 7562 
## Resampling results across tuning parameters:
## 
##   k   RMSE       Rsquared   MAE      
##    5  0.4638059  0.8046497  0.1061886
##    7  0.4881704  0.7827721  0.1184592
##    9  0.5362937  0.7404928  0.1297338
##   11  0.5490124  0.7219486  0.1384190
##   13  0.5557333  0.7095843  0.1448693
##   15  0.5562512  0.7084820  0.1489851
##   17  0.5603558  0.7044695  0.1525170
##   19  0.5720454  0.6924686  0.1568407
##   21  0.5813601  0.6820033  0.1612579
##   23  0.5887196  0.6720903  0.1644813
## 
## RMSE was used to select the optimal model using the smallest value.
## The final value used for the model was k = 5.
knn_preds <- predict(knn_fit, newdata = test_prep)

ggplot(data = NULL, aes(x = test_prep$MSRP, y = knn_preds)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Actual MSRP",
    y = "Predicted MSRP (KNN)",
    title = "Predicted vs Actual MSRP (KNN Regression)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(data = NULL, aes(x = knn_preds, y = test_prep$MSRP - knn_preds)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "blue") +
  labs(
    x = "Predicted MSRP",
    y = "Residuals (Actual - Predicted)",
    title = "Residuals vs Predicted MSRP (KNN Regression)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(data = NULL, aes(x = test_prep$MSRP - knn_preds)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "#56B4E9", color = "white") +
  labs(
    x = "Prediction Error (Residuals)",
    y = "Count",
    title = "Distribution of Prediction Errors (KNN)"
  )

Running a prediction Model that splits the data into train and test set

set.seed(123)
train_idx <- createDataPartition(auto_omit_reduced$MSRP, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_set <- auto_omit_reduced[train_idx, ]
test_set  <- auto_omit_reduced[-train_idx, ]

# Force categorical/factor levels in test to match train
cat_vars <- names(auto_omit_reduced)[sapply(auto_omit_reduced, is.factor)]
for (v in cat_vars) {
  train_set[[v]] <- factor(train_set[[v]])
  test_set[[v]]  <- factor(test_set[[v]], levels = levels(train_set[[v]]))
}

# Model formula (all variables except MSRP) - predicting log(MSRP)
predictors <- setdiff(names(auto_omit_reduced), "MSRP")
formula <- as.formula(paste("log(MSRP) ~", paste(predictors, collapse = "+")))
lm_model <- lm(formula, data = train_set)

#Handle log scale properly
log_predictions <- predict(lm_model, newdata = test_set)  # These are in LOG scale

# Create both versions for proper evaluation
test_set$Pred_log_MSRP <- log_predictions                    # Keep log scale predictions
test_set$Pred_MSRP <- exp(log_predictions)                  # Back-transform to dollar scale

# Restrict to valid predictions
valid <- !is.na(test_set$Pred_MSRP) & !is.na(test_set$MSRP)

#Calculate on both scales for proper interpretation

# === APPROACH 1: Original Dollar Scale (Business Interpretation) ===
rmse_dollars <- sqrt(mean((test_set$MSRP[valid] - test_set$Pred_MSRP[valid])^2))
mae_dollars  <- mean(abs(test_set$MSRP[valid] - test_set$Pred_MSRP[valid]))
r2_dollars   <- cor(test_set$MSRP[valid], test_set$Pred_MSRP[valid])^2

# === APPROACH 2: Log Scale (Statistically Appropriate) ===
actual_log <- log(test_set$MSRP[valid])
rmse_log <- sqrt(mean((actual_log - test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid])^2))
mae_log  <- mean(abs(actual_log - test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid]))
r2_log   <- cor(actual_log, test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid])^2

# Convert log RMSE to percentage error for easy interpretation
percentage_error <- (exp(rmse_log) - 1) * 100

cat("\n==== Results for Full Data ====\n")
## 
## ==== Results for Full Data ====
cat("=====================================================\n")
## =====================================================
cat("=== DOLLAR SCALE EVALUATION (Business Perspective) ===\n")
## === DOLLAR SCALE EVALUATION (Business Perspective) ===
cat("Test RMSE (dollars): $", format(round(rmse_dollars), big.mark = ","), "\n")
## Test RMSE (dollars): $ 36,152
cat("Test MAE (dollars):  $", format(round(mae_dollars), big.mark = ","), "\n")
## Test MAE (dollars):  $ 11,492
cat("Test R-squared:      ", round(r2_dollars, 4), "\n")
## Test R-squared:       0.626
cat("\n=== LOG SCALE EVALUATION (Statistical Perspective) ===\n")
## 
## === LOG SCALE EVALUATION (Statistical Perspective) ===
cat("Test RMSE (log):     ", round(rmse_log, 4), "\n")
## Test RMSE (log):      0.425
cat("Test MAE (log):      ", round(mae_log, 4), "\n")
## Test MAE (log):       0.3151
cat("Test R-squared:      ", round(r2_log, 4), "\n")
## Test R-squared:       0.8563
cat("Typical % Error:     ±", round(percentage_error, 1), "%\n")
## Typical % Error:     ± 53 %
cat("=====================================================\n")
## =====================================================
#Multiple properly scaled visualizations

# Plot 1: Original Dollar Scale (Actual $ vs Predicted $)
p1 <- ggplot(test_set[valid, ], aes(x = MSRP, y = Pred_MSRP)) +

  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +

  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12))

# Plot 3: Residuals vs Fitted (Proper diagnostic plot for log model)
residuals_log <- log(test_set$MSRP[valid]) - test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid]
fitted_log <- test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid]

p3 <- ggplot(data.frame(fitted = fitted_log, residuals = residuals_log), 
             aes(x = fitted, y = residuals)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "purple", size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "blue", method = "loess", size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Residuals vs Fitted Values: Log Scale Model",
       subtitle = "Diagnostic plot for checking model assumptions",
       x = "Fitted log(MSRP)",
       y = "Residuals") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12))

# Display all plots
print(p1)

print(p2)

print(p3)

## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.4236 on 9352 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.8548, Adjusted R-squared:  0.8532 
## F-statistic:   545 on 101 and 9352 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16
#No Outliers
set.seed(123)
train_idx <- createDataPartition(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers$MSRP, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_set <- auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers[train_idx, ]
test_set  <- auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers[-train_idx, ]

# Force categorical/factor levels in test to match train
cat_vars <- names(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)[sapply(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers, is.factor)]
for (v in cat_vars) {
  train_set[[v]] <- factor(train_set[[v]])
  test_set[[v]]  <- factor(test_set[[v]], levels = levels(train_set[[v]]))
}

# Model formula (all variables except MSRP) - predicting log(MSRP)
predictors <- setdiff(names(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers), "MSRP")
formula <- as.formula(paste("log(MSRP) ~", paste(predictors, collapse = "+")))
lm_model <- lm(formula, data = train_set)

#Handle log scale properly
log_predictions <- predict(lm_model, newdata = test_set)  # These are in LOG scale

# Create both versions for proper evaluation
test_set$Pred_log_MSRP <- log_predictions                    # Keep log scale predictions
test_set$Pred_MSRP <- exp(log_predictions)                  # Back-transform to dollar scale

# Restrict to valid predictions
valid <- !is.na(test_set$Pred_MSRP) & !is.na(test_set$MSRP)

#Calculate on both scales for proper interpretation

# === APPROACH 1: Original Dollar Scale (Business Interpretation) ===
rmse_dollars <- sqrt(mean((test_set$MSRP[valid] - test_set$Pred_MSRP[valid])^2))
mae_dollars  <- mean(abs(test_set$MSRP[valid] - test_set$Pred_MSRP[valid]))
r2_dollars   <- cor(test_set$MSRP[valid], test_set$Pred_MSRP[valid])^2

# === APPROACH 2: Log Scale (Statistically Appropriate) ===
actual_log <- log(test_set$MSRP[valid])
rmse_log <- sqrt(mean((actual_log - test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid])^2))
mae_log  <- mean(abs(actual_log - test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid]))
r2_log   <- cor(actual_log, test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid])^2

# Convert log RMSE to percentage error for easy interpretation
percentage_error <- (exp(rmse_log) - 1) * 100

cat("\n==== Results for No Outlier Data ====\n")
## 
## ==== Results for No Outlier Data ====
cat("=====================================================\n")
## =====================================================
cat("=== DOLLAR SCALE EVALUATION (Business Perspective) ===\n")
## === DOLLAR SCALE EVALUATION (Business Perspective) ===
cat("Test RMSE (dollars): $", format(round(rmse_dollars), big.mark = ","), "\n")
## Test RMSE (dollars): $ 19,559
cat("Test MAE (dollars):  $", format(round(mae_dollars), big.mark = ","), "\n")
## Test MAE (dollars):  $ 9,741
cat("Test R-squared:      ", round(r2_dollars, 4), "\n")
## Test R-squared:       0.7449
cat("\n=== LOG SCALE EVALUATION (Statistical Perspective) ===\n")
## 
## === LOG SCALE EVALUATION (Statistical Perspective) ===
cat("Test RMSE (log):     ", round(rmse_log, 4), "\n")
## Test RMSE (log):      0.429
cat("Test MAE (log):      ", round(mae_log, 4), "\n")
## Test MAE (log):       0.3173
cat("Test R-squared:      ", round(r2_log, 4), "\n")
## Test R-squared:       0.8461
cat("Typical % Error:     ±", round(percentage_error, 1), "%\n")
## Typical % Error:     ± 53.6 %
cat("=====================================================\n")
## =====================================================
#Multiple properly scaled visualizations

# Plot 1: Original Dollar Scale (Actual $ vs Predicted $)
p1 <- ggplot(test_set[valid, ], aes(x = MSRP, y = Pred_MSRP)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Actual vs Predicted MSRP: Dollar Scale",
       subtitle = paste0("RMSE: $", format(round(rmse_dollars), big.mark = ","), 
                        " | R² = ", round(r2_dollars, 3)),
       x = "Actual MSRP ($)",
       y = "Predicted MSRP ($)") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar_format()) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar_format()) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12))

# Plot 2: Log Scale (Both axes in log scale - STATISTICALLY CORRECT)
p2 <- ggplot(test_set[valid, ], aes(x = log(MSRP), y = Pred_log_MSRP)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "darkgreen", size = 2) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Actual vs Predicted MSRP: Log Scale",
       subtitle = paste0("RMSE: ", round(rmse_log, 3), 
                        " | Typical Error: ±", round(percentage_error, 1), "%"),
       x = "Actual log(MSRP)",
       y = "Predicted log(MSRP)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12))

# Plot 3: Residuals vs Fitted (Proper diagnostic plot for log model)
residuals_log <- log(test_set$MSRP[valid]) - test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid]
fitted_log <- test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid]

p3 <- ggplot(data.frame(fitted = fitted_log, residuals = residuals_log), 
             aes(x = fitted, y = residuals)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "purple", size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "blue", method = "loess", size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Residuals vs Fitted Values: Log Scale Model",
       subtitle = "Diagnostic plot for checking model assumptions",
       x = "Fitted log(MSRP)",
       y = "Residuals") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12))

# Display all plots
print(p1)

print(p2)

print(p3)
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

# EXPLANATION OF CORRECTIONS
cat("\n==== KEY CORRECTIONS MADE ====\n")
## 
## ==== KEY CORRECTIONS MADE ====
cat("1. PREDICTION: exp(log_predictions) to convert back to dollars\n")

cat("2. METRICS: Calculated on both scales for proper interpretation\n")
## 2. METRICS: Calculated on both scales for proper interpretation
cat("3. PLOTTING: Fixed axis scales and labels to match data\n")
## 3. PLOTTING: Fixed axis scales and labels to match data
cat("4. DIAGNOSTICS: Added proper residual plot for log model\n")
## 4. DIAGNOSTICS: Added proper residual plot for log model
cat("\n==== INTERPRETATION GUIDE ====\n")

## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.4184 on 9257 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.8497, Adjusted R-squared:  0.848 
## F-statistic: 518.1 on 101 and 9257 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16
set.seed(123)
train_idx <- createDataPartition(auto_omit_reduced$MSRP, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_set <- auto_omit_reduced[train_idx, ]
test_set  <- auto_omit_reduced[-train_idx, ]

# Force categorical/factor levels in test to match train
cat_vars <- names(auto_omit_reduced)[sapply(auto_omit_reduced, is.factor)]
for (v in cat_vars) {
  train_set[[v]] <- factor(train_set[[v]])
  test_set[[v]]  <- factor(test_set[[v]], levels = levels(train_set[[v]]))
}

# Model formula (predicting log(MSRP))
lm_model <- lm(
  log(MSRP) ~ 
    Year +
    Market.Category +
    Engine.Fuel.Type +
    Vehicle.Style +
    Transmission.Type +
    Driven_Wheels +
    city.mpg +
    Engine.HP +
    I(Engine.HP^2) +  # Quadratic (polynomial)
    Engine.HP:Vehicle.Style +
    Engine.HP:Transmission.Type +
    city.mpg:Engine.Fuel.Type,
  data = train_set
)

#Back-transform from log scale to original dollar scale
log_predictions <- predict(lm_model, newdata = test_set)
test_set$Pred_MSRP <- exp(log_predictions)  # Convert log predictions back to dollars

#log-scale predictions for log-scale evaluation
test_set$Pred_log_MSRP <- log_predictions

# Restrict to valid predictions
valid <- !is.na(test_set$Pred_MSRP) & !is.na(test_set$MSRP)

#Two approaches for proper evaluation

# Approach 1: Evaluate on Original Dollar Scale (back-transformed predictions)
rmse_dollars <- sqrt(mean((test_set$MSRP[valid] - test_set$Pred_MSRP[valid])^2))
mae_dollars  <- mean(abs(test_set$MSRP[valid] - test_set$Pred_MSRP[valid]))
r2_dollars   <- cor(test_set$MSRP[valid], test_set$Pred_MSRP[valid])^2

# Approach 2: Evaluate on Log Scale (both actual and predicted in log scale)
rmse_log <- sqrt(mean((log(test_set$MSRP[valid]) - test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid])^2))
mae_log  <- mean(abs(log(test_set$MSRP[valid]) - test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid]))
r2_log   <- cor(log(test_set$MSRP[valid]), test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid])^2

# Convert log-scale RMSE to percentage error for interpretation
percentage_error <- (exp(rmse_log) - 1) * 100

cat("\n==== Results for Full Data ====\n")

#No Outliers
set.seed(123)
train_idx <- createDataPartition(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers$MSRP, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_set <- auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers[train_idx, ]
test_set  <- auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers[-train_idx, ]

# Force categorical/factor levels in test to match train
cat_vars <- names(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)[sapply(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers, is.factor)]
for (v in cat_vars) {
  train_set[[v]] <- factor(train_set[[v]])
  test_set[[v]]  <- factor(test_set[[v]], levels = levels(train_set[[v]]))
}

# Model formula (predicting log(MSRP))
lm_model <- lm(
  log(MSRP) ~ 
    Year +
    Market.Category +
    Engine.Fuel.Type +
    Vehicle.Style +
    Transmission.Type +
    Driven_Wheels +
    city.mpg +
    Engine.HP +
    I(Engine.HP^2) +  # Quadratic (polynomial)
    Engine.HP:Vehicle.Style +
    Engine.HP:Transmission.Type +
    city.mpg:Engine.Fuel.Type,
  data = train_set
)

#Back-transform from log scale to original dollar scale
log_predictions <- predict(lm_model, newdata = test_set)
test_set$Pred_MSRP <- exp(log_predictions)  # Convert log predictions back to dollars

#log-scale predictions for log-scale evaluation
test_set$Pred_log_MSRP <- log_predictions

# Restrict to valid predictions
valid <- !is.na(test_set$Pred_MSRP) & !is.na(test_set$MSRP)

#Two approaches for proper evaluation

# Approach 1: Evaluate on Original Dollar Scale (back-transformed predictions)
rmse_dollars <- sqrt(mean((test_set$MSRP[valid] - test_set$Pred_MSRP[valid])^2))
mae_dollars  <- mean(abs(test_set$MSRP[valid] - test_set$Pred_MSRP[valid]))
r2_dollars   <- cor(test_set$MSRP[valid], test_set$Pred_MSRP[valid])^2

# Approach 2: Evaluate on Log Scale (both actual and predicted in log scale)
rmse_log <- sqrt(mean((log(test_set$MSRP[valid]) - test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid])^2))
mae_log  <- mean(abs(log(test_set$MSRP[valid]) - test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid]))
r2_log   <- cor(log(test_set$MSRP[valid]), test_set$Pred_log_MSRP[valid])^2

# Convert log-scale RMSE to percentage error for interpretation
percentage_error <- (exp(rmse_log) - 1) * 100

#Redoing Feature selection:Step Wise, Penalized Regression

# Full Model (all predictors) -- LOG TRANSFORMATION
full.model_log <- lm(log(MSRP) ~ ., data = auto_omit_reduced)
full.model_noout_log <- lm(log(MSRP) ~ ., data = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)

# Null Model (only intercept) -- LOG TRANSFORMATION

                       data = auto_omit_reduced,
                       method = "glmnet",
                       trControl = fitControl
                      )

# Predict and get residuals for log(MSRP)
preds_noout_log <- predict(glmnet_noout_log.fit, newdata = auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers)
residuals_noout_log <- log(auto_omit_reduced_no_outliers$MSRP) - preds_noout_log
df_resid_noout_log <- data.frame(Fitted = as.numeric(preds_noout_log), Residuals = as.numeric(residuals_noout_log))

# Residuals vs Fitted for log model
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(df_resid_noout_log, aes(x=Fitted, y=Residuals)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept=0, linetype="dashed", color="red") +
  labs(title = "Residuals vs Fitted | glmnet log(MSRP)")

# QQ Plot for log residuals
ggplot(data.frame(resid = residuals_noout_log), aes(sample = resid)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  labs(title = "QQ Plot of Residuals (log MSRP)")

#Non Parametric Stuff
#KNN_Full
# 1. Select features
features <- c("Year_Group", "Market.Category", "Engine.HP", "Engine.Fuel.Type", 
              "city.mpg", "Vehicle.Style", "Transmission.Type", "Driven_Wheels")
knn_data <- auto_omit_reduced %>% select(MSRP, all_of(features))

# 2. Train/test split
set.seed(123)
idx <- createDataPartition(knn_data$MSRP, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_set <- knn_data[idx, ]
test_set  <- knn_data[-idx, ]

# 3. Create dummy variables (one-hot encoding for categorical predictors)
dummies   <- dummyVars(MSRP ~ ., data = train_set)
train_enc <- predict(dummies, newdata = train_set)
test_enc  <- predict(dummies, newdata = test_set)
train_enc <- data.frame(MSRP = train_set$MSRP, train_enc)
test_enc  <- data.frame(MSRP = test_set$MSRP, test_enc)

# 4. Center/scale all numeric variables
preproc     <- preProcess(train_enc, method = c("center", "scale"))
## Warning in preProcess.default(train_enc, method = c("center", "scale")): These
## variables have zero variances:
## Market.Category.Crossover.Exotic.Luxury.Performance,
## Market.Category.Performance.Hybrid
train_prep  <- predict(preproc, newdata = train_enc)
test_prep   <- predict(preproc, newdata = test_enc)

# 5. Fit KNN on processed data
set.seed(123)
knn_fit <- train(
  MSRP ~ .,
  data = train_prep,
  method = "knn",
  tuneLength = 10,
  trControl = trainControl(method = "cv", number = 5)
)
print(knn_fit)
## k-Nearest Neighbors 
## 
## 9454 samples
##  110 predictor
## 
## No pre-processing
## Resampling: Cross-Validated (5 fold) 
## Summary of sample sizes: 7564, 7562, 7564, 7564, 7562 
## Resampling results across tuning parameters:
## 
##   k   RMSE       Rsquared   MAE      
##    5  0.4663334  0.8028459  0.1025075
##    7  0.5109343  0.7697560  0.1153919
##    9  0.5366904  0.7412358  0.1236105
##   11  0.5473996  0.7236204  0.1305546
##   13  0.5568105  0.7083058  0.1366036
##   15  0.5566971  0.7093517  0.1402476
##   17  0.5596917  0.7046850  0.1431936
##   19  0.5713060  0.6942050  0.1472993
##   21  0.5794169  0.6843602  0.1513453
##   23  0.5882983  0.6719327  0.1551623
## 
## RMSE was used to select the optimal model using the smallest value.
## The final value used for the model was k = 5.
knn_preds <- predict(knn_fit, newdata = test_prep)

ggplot(data = NULL, aes(x = test_prep$MSRP, y = knn_preds)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Actual MSRP",
    y = "Predicted MSRP (KNN)",
    title = "Predicted vs Actual MSRP (KNN Regression)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(data = NULL, aes(x = knn_preds, y = test_prep$MSRP - knn_preds)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "blue") +
  labs(
    x = "Predicted MSRP",
    y = "Residuals (Actual - Predicted)",
    title = "Residuals vs Predicted MSRP (KNN Regression)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(data = NULL, aes(x = test_prep$MSRP - knn_preds)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "#56B4E9", color = "white") +
  labs(
    x = "Prediction Error (Residuals)",
    y = "Count",
    title = "Distribution of Prediction Errors (KNN)"
  )

## RMSE was used to select the optimal model using the smallest value.
## The final value used for the model was k = 5.
knn_preds <- predict(knn_fit, newdata = test_prep)

ggplot(data = NULL, aes(x = test_prep$MSRP, y = knn_preds)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Actual MSRP",
    y = "Predicted MSRP (KNN)",
    title = "Predicted vs Actual MSRP (KNN Regression)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(data = NULL, aes(x = knn_preds, y = test_prep$MSRP - knn_preds)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "blue") +
  labs(
    x = "Predicted MSRP",
    y = "Residuals (Actual - Predicted)",
    title = "Residuals vs Predicted MSRP (KNN Regression)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(data = NULL, aes(x = test_prep$MSRP - knn_preds)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "#56B4E9", color = "white") +
  labs(
    x = "Prediction Error (Residuals)",
    y = "Count",
    title = "Distribution of Prediction Errors (KNN)"
  )

##Prediction on Train/Test Set #####
set.seed(123)
train_idx <- createDataPartition(auto_omit_reduced$MSRP, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_set <- auto_omit_reduced[train_idx, ]
test_set  <- auto_omit_reduced[-train_idx, ]

# Force categorical/factor levels in test to match train
cat_vars <- names(auto_omit_reduced)[sapply(auto_omit_reduced, is.factor)]
for (v in cat_vars) {
  train_set[[v]] <- factor(train_set[[v]])
  test_set[[v]]  <- factor(test_set[[v]], levels = levels(train_set[[v]]))
}

# Model formula (all variables except MSRP)
#predictors <- setdiff(names(auto_omit_reduced), "MSRP")
#formula <- as.formula(paste("log(MSRP) ~", paste(predictors, collapse = "+")))
lm_model <- lm(
  log(MSRP) ~ 
    Year_Group +
    Market.Category +
    Engine.Fuel.Type +
    Vehicle.Style +
    Transmission.Type +
    Driven_Wheels +
    city.mpg +
    Engine.HP +
    I(Engine.HP^2) +  # Quadratic (polynomial)
    Engine.HP:Vehicle.Style +
    Engine.HP:Transmission.Type +
    city.mpg:Engine.Fuel.Type,
  data = train_set
)

# Predict
test_set$Pred_MSRP <- predict(lm_model, newdata = test_set)

# Restrict to valid predictions
valid <- !is.na(test_set$Pred_MSRP) & !is.na(test_set$MSRP)

# Metrics (only valid rows)
rmse <- sqrt(mean((test_set$MSRP[valid] - test_set$Pred_MSRP[valid])^2))
mae  <- mean(abs(test_set$MSRP[valid] - test_set$Pred_MSRP[valid]))
r2   <- cor(test_set$MSRP[valid], test_set$Pred_MSRP[valid])^2

cat("\n==== Results for Full Data (Year_Group) ====\n")
## 
## ==== Results for Full Data (Year_Group) ====
cat("Test RMSE:", rmse, "\n")
## Test RMSE: 71602.93
cat("Test MAE:", mae, "\n")
## Test MAE: 41009.3
cat("Test R-squared:", r2, "\n")
## Test R-squared: 0.3550583
# Plot
ggplot(test_set[valid, ], aes(x = log(MSRP), y = Pred_MSRP)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Actual vs Predicted MSRP: Full Data",
       x = "Actual MSRP",
       y = "Predicted MSRP") +
  theme_minimal()
